questions.text: The Community Mortgage Program (CMP), administered by the Social Housing Finance Corporation (SHFC), is best described as what?

options.text: A housing classification defined in BP 220, which sets standards for economic and socialized housing
A delivery method that finances community purchase of land for in-place housing
A government subsidy program that provides free housing to the poor, subject to eligibility criteria
A regulation requiring all housing developments to include communal facilities, such as parks and playgrounds

rationale.a: CMP is not a classification; it is a delivery mechanism. It can deliver socialized or economic housing.
rationale.b: CMP is a delivery method where SHFC finances a community organization's collective purchase of land the community occupies or identifies. The community then repays the mortgage through the organization. It enables in-situ (in-place) upgrading without displacement.
rationale.c: Incorrect — CMP is a mortgage program, not a subsidy. Communities must repay the mortgage, though terms are favorable.
rationale.d: Incorrect — CMP is about land financing, not about facility requirements within developments.
rationale.correct: CMP is a delivery method where SHFC finances a community organization's collective purchase of land the community occupies or identifies. The community then repays the mortgage through the organization. It enables in-situ (in-place) upgrading without displacement.
rationale.takeaway: CMP is the most successful in-situ upgrading program in the Philippines because it preserves social cohesion and avoids costly relocation. It is a delivery method, not a classification or subsidy.

questions.text: A developer building a luxury residential subdivision must include socialized housing units as part of the balanced housing obligation under RA 7279 and RA 10884. Where can these socialized units be located?

options.text: Only within the same subdivision (on-site), ensuring integration with luxury units
Only in a separate location (off-site), which may be more cost-effective for developers
Either within the same subdivision or in a separate location (on-site or off-site)
In a government-owned site managed by NHA only, subject to availability and approval

rationale.a: On-site is an option, but so is off-site. The law provides developer flexibility.
rationale.b: Off-site is an option, but so is on-site. The law is not restrictive.
rationale.c: RA 7279 and RA 10884 give developers four options: (1) on-site within the project, (2) off-site in a separate location, (3) joint venture with NHA, or (4) bond contribution to NHA. On-site or off-site are both acceptable methods.
rationale.d: Incorrect — RA 7279 allows on-site, off-site, NHA partnership, or bond contribution. NHA-managed sites are only one option.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 and RA 10884 give developers four options: (1) on-site within the project, (2) off-site in a separate location, (3) joint venture with NHA, or (4) bond contribution to NHA. On-site or off-site are both acceptable methods.
rationale.takeaway: RA 7279 gives developers choice in delivery method for balanced housing. On-site keeps affordability next to market housing (mixed-income). Off-site can be less expensive to develop. Both satisfy the legal mandate.

questions.text: Under BP 220, which housing classification is defined by a minimum lot area of 100 square meters and a minimum floor area of 22 square meters?

options.text: Socialized housing (new subdivision)
Socialized housing (in-fill)
Economic housing
Low-cost housing

rationale.a: Socialized new subdivision is 72 sq.m. lot / 22 sq.m. floor, not 100/42.
rationale.b: Socialized in-fill is 28 sq.m. lot / 22 sq.m. floor, not 100/42.
rationale.c: BP 220 specifies that economic housing has a minimum lot area of 100 sq.m. and minimum floor area of 42 sq.m. These larger standards provide more livability for middle-income families.
rationale.d: Low-cost housing is not a statutory classification in BP 220; it is an industry segment. Low-cost is not defined in law.
rationale.correct: BP 220 specifies that economic housing has a minimum lot area of 100 sq.m. and minimum floor area of 22 sq.m. These larger standards provide more livability for middle-income families.
rationale.takeaway: Economic housing is the second statutory classification under BP 220. The 100/42 standard is larger than socialized (72/28 and 28/22) and reflects the target of middle-income families who can afford more space.

questions.text: A government agency directly develops and builds housing using budget allocations, targeting informal settlers and government employees on low salaries. Which delivery method is this agency using?

options.text: Balanced housing on-site development
NHA direct production
Pag-IBIG direct purchase program
Joint venture with private developers

rationale.a: Balanced housing on-site is a private developer obligation, not an NHA responsibility.
rationale.b: NHA (National Housing Authority) is the primary government producer of socialized and some economic housing. NHA directly develops using government budget, targeting informal settlers and low-income government employees. This is the definition of NHA direct production.
rationale.c: Pag-IBIG direct purchase is financing for individual buyers to purchase from private developers, not NHA-built.
rationale.d: NHA joint ventures partner with private developers but are not the only delivery method NHA uses.
rationale.correct: NHA (National Housing Authority) is the primary government producer of socialized and some economic housing. NHA directly develops using government budget, targeting informal settlers and low-income government employees. This is the definition of NHA direct production.
rationale.takeaway: NHA direct production is a core delivery method for socialized housing. It is financed through government budget, not by end-buyer loans or developer obligations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a housing classification defined by Philippine law?

options.text: Low-cost housing (per BP 220)
Pag-IBIG housing (per Pag-IBIG Fund regulations)
Socialized housing (per BP 220)
NHA-built housing (per NHA Charter)

rationale.a: Low-cost housing is not a statutory classification in BP 220; it is an industry-recognized segment between economic and open-market.
rationale.b: Pag-IBIG housing is a financing method, not a legal classification. Pag-IBIG finances socialized, economic, or open-market housing.
rationale.c: BP 220 defines socialized housing by minimum lot and floor area standards (72/28 lot, 22 floor) and target income range. This is a legal classification.
rationale.d: NHA-built housing is a delivery method (NHA is the builder), not a classification. NHA-built housing can be socialized or economic.
rationale.correct: BP 220 defines socialized housing by minimum lot area of 72 sqm (new subdivision) or smaller per type, floor area of 18 sqm and target income range. This is a legal classification.
rationale.takeaway: Classifications are fixed by law and define minimum standards. Delivery methods (how it is built, who builds it, how it is financed) are policy choices. Students frequently confuse the two.

questions.text: Which housing delivery method is LEAST preferred by government for fulfilling balanced housing obligations because it delays housing production?

options.text: On-site development of socialized units, which allows for immediate occupancy and integration into existing communities.
Off-site development of socialized units, often resulting in longer timelines due to land acquisition and infrastructure development.
Bond or cash contribution to NHA's housing fund
Joint venture with NHA, facilitating resource sharing and potentially faster project completion.

rationale.a: On-site is a preferred method that delivers housing immediately within the project.
rationale.b: Off-site is a preferred method that delivers housing in a separate but timely location.
rationale.c: Bond or cash contribution allows developers to delay housing production by contributing money to NHA instead of building units. NHA must then use the fund to construct housing, which takes additional time and resources. Government prefers on-site, off-site, or NHA partnership because these deliver housing faster.
rationale.d: NHA partnership directly builds housing; it does not delay production like a bond.
rationale.correct: Bond or cash contribution allows developers to delay housing production by contributing money to NHA instead of building units. NHA must then use the fund to construct housing, which takes additional time and resources. Government prefers on-site, off-site, or NHA partnership because these deliver housing faster.
rationale.takeaway: The bond contribution option exists as a fallback when on-site and off-site are infeasible, but government considers it the least desirable. Immediate housing delivery (on-site/off-site) is preferred.

questions.text: A private developer plans to fulfill its balanced housing obligation by building 80 units of socialized housing off-site in a different city. The developer constructs the units to meet BP 220 standards (28 sq.m. lot, 22 sq.m. floor for infill). Which statement is true?

options.text: This cannot be considered balanced housing because off-site units are always considered a separate project classification.
This is balanced housing delivery off-site, and the units are classified as socialized housing because they meet BP 220 standards.
This is balanced housing delivery, but the units become economic housing because they are built by a private developer, not the government.
This is balanced housing delivery only if the developer also builds open-market housing in the same location.

rationale.a: Incorrect — Off-site is explicitly permitted by RA 7279 as a balanced housing option. Location does not determine classification.
rationale.b: Off-site is a valid balanced housing delivery option under RA 7279. The classification of the units depends on BP 220 standards, not on location or developer type. If they meet BP 220 socialized standards (28 sq.m. lot, 22 sq.m. floor), they are socialized housing regardless of being built off-site by a private developer.
rationale.c: Incorrect — Classification is determined by BP 220 standards, not by developer type. Private developers can build socialized housing.
rationale.d: Incorrect — Off-site balanced housing does not require the developer to also build open-market housing. The developer is fulfilling its obligation through off-site alone.
rationale.correct: Off-site is a valid balanced housing delivery option under RA 7279. The classification of the units depends on BP 220 standards, not on location or developer type. If they meet BP 220 socialized standards (e.g., 36 sqm lot rowhouse, 18 sqm floor minimum), they are socialized housing regardless of being built off-site by a private developer.
rationale.takeaway: Students must separate classification (BP 220 standards) from delivery method (on-site/off-site/etc.). A private developer building to BP 220 standards is building socialized housing, even if it is off-site and even if the main project is open-market.

questions.text: A private developer builds a 200-unit residential subdivision marketed as 'economic housing.' The developer finances the project through Pag-IBIG. Which statement is correct?

options.text: This is Pag-IBIG housing, not economic housing, because of the financing source.
This is economic housing because it meets the BP 220 standards, regardless of the financing method.
This is a joint venture between the developer and Pag-IBIG, so it cannot be classified as economic.
This is socialized housing because Pag-IBIG-financed housing is required to be socialized by law.

rationale.a: Incorrect — Pag-IBIG is a financing method, not a classification. The classification is determined by the physical standards, not the money source.
rationale.b: Housing classification is determined by BP 220 minimum standards (lot area, floor area, target income), not by the financing source. Pag-IBIG is a delivery mechanism; the classification remains economic if it meets the 100 sq.m. lot / 42 sq.m. floor standards.
rationale.c: Incorrect — Pag-IBIG is a single finance agency, not a separate partner classification. The developer is the builder; Pag-IBIG provides money.
rationale.d: Incorrect — Pag-IBIG finances socialized, economic, and low-cost housing. It does not require all its financed projects to be socialized.
rationale.correct: Housing classification is determined by BP 220 minimum standards (lot area, floor area, target income), not by the financing source. Pag-IBIG is a delivery mechanism; the classification remains economic if it meets the 100 sq.m. lot / 22 sq.m. floor standards.
rationale.takeaway: This is the most frequently tested concept: Classification ≠ Delivery Method. A given classification can use multiple delivery methods. Economic housing can be Pag-IBIG-financed, bank-financed, or NHA-built without changing its classification.

questions.text: A 500-unit residential development is classified as open-market housing and costs ₱2 billion to develop. According to RA 10884, the developer must produce socialized housing equivleant to at least what cost amount?

options.text: ₱100 million (5% of project cost)
₱200 million (10% of project cost)
₱300 million (15% of project cost)
₱400 million (20% of project cost)

rationale.a: 5% is below the 15–20% threshold mandated by RA 10884.
rationale.b: 10% is below the 15–20% threshold mandated by RA 10884.
rationale.c: RA 10884 requires balanced housing equivalent to 15–20% of project cost. The minimum is 15%; therefore, 15% of ₱2 billion = ₱300 million worth of socialized housing must be produced.
rationale.d: 20% (₱400 million) is the maximum of the range; the minimum is 15%. Either is compliant, but 15% is the floor.
rationale.correct: RA 10884 requires balanced housing equivalent to 15–20% of project cost. The minimum is 15%; therefore, 15% of ₱2 billion = ₱300 million worth of socialized housing must be produced.
rationale.takeaway: RA 10884 specifies 15–20% of project cost. Students must be able to calculate the actual amount for a given project size. Both 15% and 20% are compliant; neither is 'wrong,' but 15% is the minimum.

questions.text: A urban poor community living on informal land occupies 2 hectares. Instead of being evicted and relocated, the community is enabled to collectively purchase the land through an SHFC mortgage. The community will then develop the land incrementally using Pag-IBIG financing for individual home improvements. What housing classification and delivery method best describes this scenario?

options.text: Economic housing classification, delivered through Community Mortgage Program (CMP)
Socialized housing classification, delivered through Community Mortgage Program (CMP)
Low-cost housing classification, delivered through NHA direct production
Open-market housing classification, delivered through Pag-IBIG direct purchase

rationale.a: CMP can target socialized or economic, but informal settlers are socialized housing beneficiaries. Economic would be middle-income, not informal settlers.
rationale.b: The community is informal settlers, meaning they target socialized housing eligibility (low income). CMP is the delivery method (SHFC financing for collective land purchase). The classification is socialized, and the delivery is CMP, which enables in-situ development without relocation.
rationale.c: Incorrect — Low-cost is industry-recognized but not a statutory classification. NHA would be direct production, not CMP. CMP is SHFC-administered.
rationale.d: Incorrect — Informal settlers are not open-market; Pag-IBIG direct purchase is for individual buyers purchasing completed units, not for community land acquisition.
rationale.correct: The community is informal settlers, meaning they target socialized housing eligibility (low income). CMP is the delivery method (SHFC financing for collective land purchase). The classification is socialized, and the delivery is CMP, which enables in-situ development without relocation.
rationale.takeaway: CMP is uniquely valuable for informal settlements because it enables in-place upgrading. The classification of the eventual housing depends on the community's income and the unit standards, but the delivery method is what makes CMP unique.
